key_insight: Long-range ML interatomic potentials better capture electrostatic defect interactions in SrTiO3 than a short-range baseline, especially when tested beyond idealized charge models into realistic DFT defect energetics.
engineering_relevance: Accurate defect energetics and migration barriers in perovskites are essential for predicting reliability, transport, and functional behavior in oxide materials.
method: Benchmarked MACE-POLAR, MACE-LES, and LOREM against short-range MACE
Progressed from synthetic point-charge systems to first-principles SrTiO3 defect structures
Evaluated Sr-O Schottky vacancy pairs and oxygen-vacancy migration via CI-NEB and MD
evidence_signal: The study compares models on both idealized electrostatic test cases and DFT-based SrTiO3 defect data, including vacancy-pair separations and migration-barrier trends.
watch_item: Performance may still be constrained by DFT energy complexity, since dielectric screening and exchange-correlation effects can obscure pure long-range electrostatics in training and evaluation.
paper_title: Long-Range Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials for Defect Energetics in SrTiO$_3$
